title: I made shaders compile 4-10x faster - unreal enigne as proof
author: bazingaboi22
selftext:
[https://zdxc.org](https://zdxc.org)

If you're not familiar with the topic, directxshadercompiler- is the shader compiler that drives unreal engine, and its incredibly slow. I had a theory that it could be an order of magnitude faster if you ditch llvm.  
  
Crazy to see that it is possible prove such theories now in an incredibly short amount of time. Been tinkering with it for only a month, it started out as a little hand coded lab experiment to emit dxil. But progress went crazy when I just let the LLMs start ripping through feature support.  
  
It should be a drop-in replacement for any game engine that uses directx, and should massively speed up shader compilation times in unreal 5.8

As with any new compiler project, please let me know of any bugs or miscompiles or glitches.

comments.author: mbreaddit
comments.body:
Shader compilation might be impressive, but do they also **perform equally good**? 

While i get shader compilation is annoying i need to make sure the shaders work and perform good, which has higher priority as i usualy don´t compile 12k shaders all day long but only a handful a day.

replies.author: bazingaboi22
replies.body:
It should have similar if not outright equal performance my testing in unreal seems to back that up. ymmv, let me know.

dxil is an /intermediate/ format which already gets lowered into isa by a second optimization pass being done by the gpu's drivers

To be honest leaving the optimization up to the driver is kind of the whole point of dxil
